- When sentiment is positive (≥0.2) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; adjust forecast downward by 1–3% for the next 5–7 days.
- When sentiment is negative (≤-0.2), model often underestimates; increase forecast by 1–3% for the next 5–7 days.
- After a sharp price spike (≥5% from prior peak), model frequently overshoots in the following 3–5 days; reduce forecast by 2–5% for the next 3–7 days.
- Model consistently underestimates mean-reversion periods (e.g., after 60+ days of upward trend); add 0.5–1.5% buffer to forecast for 10–15 day horizon.
- For 30-day forecasts, model often misses late-cycle peaks; shift forecast upward by 1–3% if sentiment is neutral or slightly positive in last 3–5 days.
- If sentiment history shows alternating +/– signals, model tends to lag; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast for 1–3 day horizon to catch momentum.
